basic_information.official_title: AN ACT RECONSTITUTING THE PARLIAMENTARY DISTRICTS IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 58, ENTITLED “AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF THE PARLIAMENTARY DISTRICTS IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO”
signed_by: Atty. Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker (signed “FOR” by another hand on the captured copy)
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately upon publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or on its official website

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Redraws the region's entire electoral map. The 32 parliamentary districts remain, but Sulu's seven are gone and every other province, Cotabato City and the Special Geographic Area gains at least 1 seat.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act does not state a reason. Its own transitory provision speaks of Sulu “rejoining” the BARMM, which indicates the province is no longer part of the region — and its seven districts are accordingly redistributed.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Basilan goes from 3 districts to 4, Lanao del Sur 8 to 9, both Maguindanao provinces 4 to 5, Tawi-Tawi 3 to 4, Cotabato City 2 to 3, and the Special Geographic Area 1 to 2. Sulu has none.
who_will_be_affected: Every voter in the BARMM — your district has almost certainly changed
Candidates in the 2025 Bangsamoro Parliamentary Election
Residents of the Special Geographic Area, whose representation doubles
Sulu, which holds no parliamentary districts under this map
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in 2025. Read alongside BAA 86, which provided for apportionment in 2026.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Still 32 districts, but the map is completely redrawn: Sulu's 7 seats are gone and every remaining area gains at least one. Check your district again.
in_practice: 32 single-member parliamentary districts, on a stated regional population of 4,545,486

Basilan 4 districts (541,947) · Lanao del Sur 9 (1,368,137) · Maguindanao del Norte 5 (741,428) · Maguindanao del Sur 5 (813,243) · Tawi-Tawi 4 (482,645) · Special Geographic Area 2 (214,703) · City of Cotabato 3 (383,383)
Sulu holds no parliamentary districts under this act
If Sulu rejoins the BARMM, Congress may allocate at least seven district seats to it
For the 2025 election, candidates who already filed keep their candidacy in the district where they originally filed, even if their home barangay moved to another district
Voting takes place only within the boundaries as redrawn by this act
If a new district has no elected representative after the candidacy deadline, the President of the Philippines appoints an interim representative

for_specific_groups.Voters: Your district has very likely changed. Municipalities have been regrouped across the whole region, not only where seats were added.
for_specific_groups.Residents of the Special Geographic Area: Your representation doubles — from a single Lone District to two districts, splitting the eight municipalities into a 1st and 2nd District.
for_specific_groups.Cotabato City: Three districts instead of two, drawn barangay by barangay.
for_specific_groups.Sulu: The province holds no parliamentary districts under this map. Section 3 contemplates its return.
for_specific_groups.Candidates in the 2025 election: You keep your candidacy where you filed, even if your registered barangay has been reassigned — but voting happens only inside the new boundaries.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The BARMM as constituted under this act.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: At the 2025 Bangsamoro Parliamentary Election and after.
what_you_can_do: Check your municipality against the new district lists — do not rely on the BAA 58 map
Ask COMELEC for the implementing guidelines it is directed to issue for the 2025 election
Read BAA 86, which followed this act on apportionment
watch_out_for: The act gives no reason for Sulu's removal. Its language of “rejoining” is the only indication of the province's status.
Restoring Sulu's seats is assigned to Congress, not to the Bangsamoro Parliament.
An interim representative for a new district is appointed by the President of the Philippines — an unelected seat filled from Manila.
Candidates may end up representing a district in which they are not registered to vote, under the 2025 transition rule.
The Special Geographic Area table is headed “Barangay” but lists municipalities.

key_terms_explained.Redistricting: Redrawing the boundaries of electoral districts.
key_terms_explained.Reapportionment: Redistributing the number of seats among areas.
key_terms_explained.COC: Certificate of Candidacy — the formal filing that makes someone a candidate.
key_terms_explained.Interim representative: A person appointed to hold a seat until an election fills it.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Safar 24, 1447 / 19 August 2025, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 28 August 2025.

benefits.headline: A rebalanced map — every remaining area of the region gains representation.

direct_benefits.benefit: Two districts for the Special Geographic Area instead of one
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Residents of the eight SGA municipalities
direct_benefits.how_to_access: 1st District: Kadayangan, Nabalawag, Pahamuddin, Tugunan. 2nd District: Malidegao, Ligawasan, Old Kaabakan, Kapalawan

direct_benefits.benefit: An additional district for Basilan, Lanao del Sur, both Maguindanao provinces, Tawi-Tawi and Cotabato City
Continuity of candidacy for those who had already filed

indirect_benefits: Published population figures for every district, allowing the apportionment to be checked
A stated route for Sulu's seats to be restored if it rejoins
limitations: No reason given for the removal of Sulu's districts.
Restoration of those seats rests with Congress.
Interim representatives are appointed by the President rather than elected.

for_citizens: None. The act redraws boundaries; it imposes no duty.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections, which is directed to issue guidelines implementing the new districting for the 2025 election
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no challenge or complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A voter in Sumisip, Basilan finds their municipality now in the 3rd District with Ungkaya Pukan and Tabuan Lasa — a different grouping from the 2024 map.
A resident of Ligawasan in the Special Geographic Area now votes in the SGA's 2nd District rather than a single lone district covering all eight municipalities.

A candidate filed a Certificate of Candidacy before the redistricting, and their home barangay has since been moved to another district. Section 5 lets them keep their candidacy where they filed, though voting occurs only within the new boundaries.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Parliamentary Redistricting Act of 2025”.

Section 2 — Amends Section 4 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 58, reapportioning the thirty-two single-member parliamentary districts against a stated BARMM population of 4,545,486: Basilan 4 districts (541,947); Lanao del Sur 9 (1,368,137); Maguindanao del Norte 5 (741,428); Maguindanao del Sur 5 (813,243); Tawi-Tawi 4 (482,645); the Special Geographic Area 2 (214,703); and the City of Cotabato 3 (383,383), enumerated barangay by barangay. Sulu, which held seven districts under BAA 58, has none under this act.

Section 3 — Transitory provision: in the event that the province of Sulu rejoins the BARMM, Congress may allocate at least seven Parliamentary District Seats corresponding to the population and other equitable requirements of the law.

Section 4 — Interim representation: where the act creates a new parliamentary district after the deadline for filing Certificates of Candidacy for the immediately forthcoming parliamentary elections, and the district is left without a duly elected representative, the President of the Philippines shall appoint an Interim Parliamentary District Representative with the same rights, duties and privileges as an elected representative, whose term ends automatically when the duly elected representative assumes office after the next regular or special elections.

Section 5 — Effect of the new redistricting: for the 2025 BARMM Parliamentary Election, aspirants who have filed their Certificate of Candidacy retain their candidacy in the district where they originally filed, notwithstanding that the barangay where they are registered has been reassigned to a different district, provided that voting takes place only within the boundaries as defined by this act. The Commission on Elections shall issue appropriate implementing guidelines.
Section 8 — Takes effect immediately upon publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or on its official website.

who_benefits: Voters in Basilan, Lanao del Sur, both Maguindanao provinces, Tawi-Tawi, Cotabato City and the Special Geographic Area
Residents of the Special Geographic Area, whose seats double

related_legislation.related_note: Amends Section 4 of BAA 58, the original parliamentary districts act. Followed by BAA 86 on the apportionment of parliamentary districts. The Special Geographic Area municipalities it lists were created by BAA 41–47, and this act confirms Ligawasan among them.

implementation_status.irr_status: Section 5 directs COMELEC to issue implementing guidelines for the 2025 Bangsamoro Parliamentary Election.
implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. The act gives no reason for the removal of Sulu's districts; its transitory provision refers to Sulu “rejoining” the BARMM. Whether and when Sulu's seats are restored is a matter the act assigns to Congress. Read alongside BAA 86 for the position after 2026.

citizen_questions.a: Almost certainly. The whole map was redrawn — municipalities were regrouped across every province, not only where seats were added. Check the lists in this act rather than the 2024 map in BAA 58.

citizen_questions.q: What happened to Sulu's seven districts?
citizen_questions.a: They are not in this map. The act gives no reason, but its transitory provision speaks of Sulu “rejoining” the BARMM, which indicates the province is no longer part of the region.

citizen_questions.q: Could Sulu get its seats back?
citizen_questions.a: Section 3 says that if Sulu rejoins the BARMM, Congress may allocate at least seven Parliamentary District Seats to it. Notably that power is given to Congress, not to the Bangsamoro Parliament.

citizen_questions.q: Did the Special Geographic Area gain anything?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. It goes from a single Lone District to two — the 1st covering Kadayangan, Nabalawag, Pahamuddin and Tugunan, and the 2nd covering Malidegao, Ligawasan, Old Kaabakan and Kapalawan.

citizen_questions.q: I filed as a candidate before this passed. What now?
citizen_questions.a: Section 5 lets you retain your candidacy in the district where you originally filed, even if the barangay where you are registered has moved to another district. Voting happens only within the new boundaries.

citizen_questions.q: Who fills a new district that has no elected representative?
citizen_questions.a: The President of the Philippines appoints an Interim Parliamentary District Representative, whose term ends when a duly elected representative takes office after the next regular or special elections.
